en.title: 10 Must-Watch Netflix Arrivals Hitting Your Screen in November 2026
en.summary: Netflix is dropping a treasure trove of new movies and shows this November, from awards-season contenders to gripping dramas and much-needed laughs.
en.body:
## 1. Possible Love
Director Lee Chang-dong, the visionary behind "Burning," returns with this sweeping drama that explores the complexities of marriage across different socioeconomic strata. It's a deep dive into human connection that promises to be an awards-season frontrunner, especially after its acclaimed Cannes debut.

## 2. The Mosquito Bowl
Peter Berg directs this World War II epic, which isn't just about football but about the camaraderie and resilience of Marines during wartime. Expect the signature gritty realism Berg is known for, combined with a powerful underdog story.

## 3. The Body
This teen horror series is set to deliver chills and thrills, diving into the darker corners of teenage life. If you're looking for a supernatural scare with a contemporary edge, this is your go-to.

## 4. Murder in Galicia
Step into the shoes of a detective in this gripping crime series set against the atmospheric backdrop of Galicia. It's a must-watch for fans of intricate mysteries and compelling procedural storytelling.

## 5. The Altruists
This intriguing drama delves into the lives of individuals driven by a desire to help others, exploring the blurred lines between altruism and obsession. It's a character-driven piece that promises complex moral questions.

## 6. Heartland (2026)
Starring the always-brilliant Jessica Chastain, this drama is poised to be a quiet powerhouse, exploring themes of family, resilience, and the enduring spirit. Keep an eye on Chastain's performance; it's bound to be a highlight.

## 7. Gentle Monster (2026)
Get ready for a visually stunning animated action-comedy that promises big laughs and even bigger set pieces. This one's for anyone craving pure, unadulterated entertainment with a creative flair.

## 8. Mike Tyson: Return of the Mike
This documentary offers an unfiltered look into the life and career of the legendary boxer. For fans of sports documentaries, this is an essential watch, promising raw honesty and captivating insights.

## 9. Bass X Machina
Prepare for a unique cinematic experience with "Bass X Machina," a film that blends music, technology, and human emotion. Its experimental approach is sure to spark conversation among cinephiles.

## 10. The Empress – Season 3
The lavish historical drama returns, continuing the saga of one of history's most captivating figures. Expect more political intrigue, stunning costumes, and dramatic personal entanglements as the empress navigates her reign.
Bottom Line: November on Netflix is a cinematic feast, offering a diverse range of stories from award-bait dramas to edge-of-your-seat thrillers.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix Netflix is finally releasing movies again. After a pretty abysmal October on the Original front (with Animals from Ben Affleck literally carrying the entire month’s weight on its back), we’ve got a stacked lineup with new animated titles, awards hopefuls and more plus lots of licensed movies including some of the biggest movies of the year. Let’s dive in.  November on Netflix usually means one thing: Christmas movies, and lots of them. This year is no different, with a sleigh-load of holiday romances landing throughout the month, but we’re leaving the tinsel to one side for this list (our full holiday guide has you covered there). Instead, we’re focusing on the best of everything else. Netflix’s awards-season push is in full swing, with a new film from one of Korea’s greatest living directors, a Ron Howard documentary, a Cannes competition title starring Léa Seydoux, and Peter Berg’s big WWII football epic. On the licensed side, we’ve got Chris Rock’s return to directing, Zoey Deutch hunting down Jon Hamm, Curry Barker’s record-breaking Obsession , Teyana Taylor’s breakout performance, and Mario heading to space. As always, we’ve split the list into new Netflix Originals first, followed by the best licensed titles. This list is primarily for Netflix in the United States, so availability in your region may vary. For everything else arriving this month, check out our full list of what’s coming to Netflix in November 2026 . Best New Netflix Original Movies in November Possible Love Director: Lee Chang-dong Cast: Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung, Cho Yeo-jeong Genre: Drama | Runtime: 164 Minutes Now Playing Eight long years after Burning , Lee Chang-dong is finally back, and Netflix has the film. Possible Love follows two middle-aged married couples from very different economic undoubtedly scored the year’s best foreign language film” , singling out a powerhouse lead performance from Jeon Do-yeon and Lee’s patient, near-wordless visual storytelling with cinematographer Kim Ji-yong. Fair warning: at nearly three hours, this is a slow-burn watch. But if you loved Burning , Parasite ‘s class commentary, or Drive My Car , clear an evening for this one. It’s very likely to be Netflix’s big International Feature contender come Oscar season. Once you’re done, Lee’s 1997 debut Green Fish is also new to Netflix this month. Heartland Director: Shana Feste Cast: Jessica Chastain, Garrett Hedlund, Carter Faith, Ross Lynch, Paul Sparks, Jennifer Nettles, John Hawkes Genre: Mystery, Thriller | Runtime: [TBC] Minutes Coming to Netflix : November 13th No, not that Heartland . This one has no connection to the long-running Canadian horse ranch drama and is instead a gritty country-music mystery from Country Strong writer-director Shana Feste.
